traditions.name: Sacred Name and Hebrew Roots movements
traditions.earliest_attestation: 1930s CE (C. O. Dodd's magazine The Faith, from 1937)
traditions.scholarly_note: Grew out of the Church of God (Seventh Day) in the early 20th century; C. O. Dodd kept the festivals from 1928 and published The Faith from 1937. Angelo Traina's Holy Name New Testament (1950) and Holy Name Bible (1962) restore the name in the King James text. Groups disagree on the form of the name: older assemblies write Yahweh (Assemblies of Yahweh, 1969) and Yahshua; many newer Hebrew Roots teachers write Yahuah and Yahusha. Scholars reconstruct the Tetragrammaton as Yahweh; the full name's vowels were never written down, and the Yahu- element in personal names (Eliyahu, Yehonatan) is attested but does not by itself fix the full name.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1930s CE (Sacred Name movement, which first wrote Yahweh); Yahuah is a later Hebrew Roots spelling
primary_sources: Exodus 3:15 ("this is my name for ever")
deities.summary: Yahuah is the personal name of the Creator, written YHWH in the Hebrew Scriptures nearly 7,000 times and replaced in most Bibles by "the LORD". The name must be restored and called upon, not hidden behind titles. The Yahu- heard in Eliyahu, Yeshayahu and in the name of his Son, Yahusha ("Yahuah saves"), keeps the sound of the Father's name. His people keep the seventh-day Sabbath, the appointed feasts and the food laws of the Torah.

deities.earliest_attestation: 1930s CE (as Yahshua); Yahusha / Yahushua are later Hebrew Roots spellings
primary_sources: John 5:43 ("I am come in my Father's name")
deities.summary: Yahusha is the Messiah, the Son of Yahuah, whose Hebrew name (the same as Joshua's) means "Yahuah saves". He came in his Father's name, kept the Torah and the feasts, died and was raised. The name Jesus, carried from Hebrew through Greek and Latin into English, lost the Yahu- that points to the Father.

add_alternate_names: Jehovah (YHWH with the vowels of Adonai)

facets.facet_name: The Name to Be Restored and Called Upon
facets.core_claim: The Creator has one personal name, Yahuah, given at the burning bush to be remembered for ever; replacing it with titles broke the third commandment, and calling on it restores the covenant.

facets.facet_name: The One Father, Not a Trinity
facets.core_claim: Yahuah alone is the Most High, the Father; Yahusha is his Son and Messiah, not a second person of a Trinity.

facets.facet_name: The Son Who Came in His Father's Name
facets.core_claim: Yahusha came in his Father's name: the Yahu- in his own name carries it, and salvation is in that name.

basis: Two vocalisations of the same four letters YHWH
Same covenant God of Sinai; Yahweh is the scholarly reconstruction, Yahuah the Sacred Name / Hebrew Roots form
parallels.source_tradition: Sacred Name and Hebrew Roots movements

basis: Jehovah and Yahuah are two renderings of YHWH
Both movements teach that the name must be used and made known, and both reject the Trinity
Yahawah (Hebrew Israelite) and Yahuah (Sacred Name) are rival vocalisations of YHWH
Same God of Israel, called by a restored Hebrew name and served by keeping the Torah
Jah / Yah is the short form of the name (Psalm 68:4, Hallelu-jah)
Same Most High, named by the short form in Rastafari and the full form in the Sacred Name movement
One God, the Father, not a Trinity
The Son is the Messiah sent by the Father
Yahusha / Yahshua and Jesus render the same Hebrew name (Yehoshua / Yeshua, Greek Iēsous)
Same Messiah, named in Hebrew form by Sacred Name believers
Both non-trinitarian movements see the Son as subordinate to the Father
Both stress the divine name the Son came to make known
